lesson: Before a heavy run, compute every part of the registered statistic that stored data already fixes. Here the stored companion row gave the cube parts at four lengths, decided the question before the run, and showed the registered second size (6,10,2) to be off resonance, so its threshold test is vacuous. Summing over primes first into a weight-independent table (new kernel ffy.c, identical to all stored rows) made the 48 seeded vectors free and cut cost per prime by 15.
